features.description: MVP mount/unmount loop: start with explicit skills and adapter none mounts exactly those packages; finish removes the workdir and records unmounted=true
steps: Run: lunchbox start --library testdata/skills --skill demo-review --skill demo-scan --adapter none
Verify the workdir contains exactly demo-review and demo-scan
Run: lunchbox finish
Verify the workdir is gone and result.json has unmounted=true

features.description: doctor reports adapter, skill dirs, counts, menu_tokens estimate, and duplicates read-only, without mounting anything
steps: Run: lunchbox doctor against a configured fake tree
Verify skill count and estimated menu_tokens match the tree
Verify no run dir or workdir was created

features.description: TUI doctor screen: navigable doctor report behind the tui cargo feature, with a --json twin and a passing snapshot test
steps: Launch the doctor TUI against a fake tree with the tui feature enabled
Verify displayed counts/tokens equal the doctor --json output for the same tree
Verify the TestBackend snapshot test passes in CI without a terminal

features.description: TUI token-cost preview: menu_tokens for a candidate pack vs without-Lunchbox, with --json twin and snapshot test
steps: Open the preview screen for a candidate pack of two demo skills
Verify the shown run estimate equals CLI estimation for that pack and the without-Lunchbox figure equals doctor's
Verify the snapshot test passes headless

features.description: TUI skill picker: browse the library, compose a pack, start a real run, finish it — all from the screen
steps: Open the picker against testdata/skills
Select demo-review and demo-scan and start the run from the screen
Finish the run from the screen and verify the workdir is gone

features.description: TUI policy review: view allow/deny per config layer and edit one; the edit persists to exactly that layer
steps: Open policy review in a project that has both global and project layers
Add a deny entry from the screen while viewing the project layer
Verify ./lunchbox.toml contains the entry and ~/.lunchbox/config.toml is unchanged
Verify the run resolver now denies that skill name

features.description: Pi Path A isolation: start spawns pi with --no-skills and --skill <workdir> present in argv; selftest guards flag drift
steps: Run: lunchbox start --library testdata/skills --skill demo-review --adapter pi --wait -- -- pi --list-models
Verify the audit spawn event shows --no-skills and --skill <workdir> in argv
Verify the adapter selftest passes (skipped cleanly if pi is absent)

features.description: v1 exit bar: scripted MVP CLI loop plus a human walkthrough of all four TUI screens against real state
steps: Verify feature-001 through feature-007 all pass
Perform the human walkthrough: doctor on real dirs, picker → start → finish, policy edit persisting to the right layer
Record walkthrough result and date in PROGRESS.md

features.description: v1 README per DESIGN §25: one-liner, install, doctor/start/finish quick start, menu_tokens before/after, not-a-skill-manager note, TUI section
steps: Every README command runs verbatim against a fresh clone with a temp HOME and the shown output matches
Install section names cargo install --locked --git (placeholder URL, no remote configured) and the from-a-clone path
README states it is not a skill manager and points --library at Kitter / Skills Manager / ~/.agents/skills

features.description: Omp Path A: start --adapter omp spawns omp with discovery off and the run workdir as the only skill source — or refuses Path A explicitly if isolation cannot be verified (DESIGN §13)
steps: adapters lists omp with version and a passing selftest where omp is installed, skipped cleanly where absent
start --adapter omp --dry-run prints the exact spawn argv including the per-run --config overlay whose content points skills.customDirectories at the workdir
A live spawn loads exactly the mounted skills (foreign pantry names absent), or the adapter refuses to spawn with an explicit error naming the probe result

features.description: `--from manifest.toml` multi-worker runs mount per-worker packs under workdir/packs/<worker> with per-worker lock mapping and budget (DESIGN §9/§11/§24)
steps: start --from <manifest> with two workers mounts workdir/packs/<worker>/ containing exactly each worker's pack; the lock lists every worker name sharing each skill; why reports each worker's pack
Invalid manifests fail closed with no run dir left behind: unknown key, schema != 1, no workers, duplicate worker name, empty pack, --skill combined with --from
The token budget is enforced per worker pack (DESIGN §10) and the offending worker is named in the error

features.description: Path B run-local agents: multi-worker starts write runs/<id>/agents/<worker>.md pointing at the worker's pack; omp loads them for the invocation only or the adapter prints the files plus an include hint (DESIGN §14 fallback); standing agent dirs are never written
steps: A two-worker start writes agents/<worker>.md per DESIGN §14 (pi-subagents frontmatter: inheritSkills false, skillPath -> the worker's pack dir, explicit skills list) and teardown removes agents/
omp loads the run-local agents for this invocation only (live-verified, foreign agents absent) or prints the files and the include hint and claims no load — audit records which
adapters --explain states each adapter's Path B belief; ~/.pi/agent and ~/.omp/agent are byte-identical before and after a Path B run

features.description: scan_command policy gate: a configured scanner runs per locked skill before mount, non-zero exit fails closed, --override-scan is explicit and audited, and the lock records the real per-skill outcome (DESIGN §10/§17)
steps: A configured scan_command runs once per locked skill as `sh -c '<scan_command> "$1"' sh <package-source>` before mount; non-zero exit fails the start with the skill, command, and exit code named and no run dir left behind

--override-scan proceeds past a failed scan, records scan = "overridden" for the offending skills, prints a warning, and the audit records both the failure and the override; the TUI picker cannot override

The lock records scan = "pass" only when a scanner exited zero, "none" when scan_command is empty, and "overridden" after an override; scanner output is captured so start --json stays a single JSON line; doctor and tui preview never scan

features.description: Thin git acquisition (ADR-0006): lunchbox add clones a skills repo into the managed pantry root ~/.lunchbox/pantry which resolve/doctor search, and update fast-forwards it
steps: add <url> clones into ~/.lunchbox/pantry/<name>, auto-detects the pantry root (repo root if root children hold SKILL.md, else exactly one first-level subdir that does; --path overrides and is recorded in <name>.path), and the skills are immediately resolvable: doctor lists the pantry and start mounts a skill with no --library

update [name] runs git pull --ff-only per managed repo and fails loudly on divergence; add removes its clone when detection fails; a broken pantry fails start closed naming the pantry while doctor reports the error without failing

no pantries configured → doctor and start outputs unchanged except the new git row; add/update fail closed when git is absent; managed pantries never enter the without-Lunchbox estimate and always lose first-wins to user library_paths

features.description: Driver Skill: skills/lunchbox/SKILL.md teaches a mounted agent to drive the lunchbox CLI (mount a sealed set, spawn the worker, always unmount) and is itself a valid pantry member acquirable via add
steps: skills/lunchbox/SKILL.md exists with name lunchbox frontmatter and teaches the run loop: doctor to see cost, start with explicit pins, worker sees only the mount, finish always (fail-closed semantics and teardown discipline stated)
It is a valid pantry member: start --library skills --skill lunchbox --adapter none mounts exactly it from a clone and finish unmounts
It is acquirable: lunchbox add <this repository's url> auto-detects the skills/ subdirectory as the pantry root, and start --skill lunchbox resolves with no --library

features.description: start fails closed with no pins: zero --skill pins and no --from error loudly and leave no run directory instead of mounting an empty set and spawning the default adapter
steps: start with no pins in plain, --json, and --dry-run forms exits non-zero with a message naming the fix (--skill <name>[@sha256:<64 hex>], --from <manifest>, or lunchbox menu) and creates no run directory and spawns nothing
pinned runs are unchanged: runs with at least one --skill or a --from manifest keep identical output shape, spawn behavior, and exit codes
failing and regression test arms cover all three forms and the pinned paths; cargo test green in both feature configurations

features.description: lunchbox menu: a single interactive TUI app (tui cargo features) with Pantry, Manifests, Doctor, and Policy screens, start-from-selection behind an explicit confirmation, replacing and removing the tui <screen> subcommands (breaking, released as 0.3.0; ADR-0007)
steps: lunchbox menu opens a full-screen mode-stack app behind the tui features (CLI-only builds error with a rebuild hint); bare lunchbox and every other subcommand stay non-interactive with no TTY detection anywhere

Pantry screen sections for managed pantries (healthy/broken), library_paths, and default .agents/skills roots with counts and duplicates; the focused root's skills list; selecting skills and confirming on a screen showing adapter, exact skills+hashes, and token cost starts a run through the same code path as CLI start

Manifests screen lists manifests discovered in ./lunchbox/manifests/*.toml then ~/.lunchbox/manifests/*.toml (project wins on name collision) with task, worker count, and token estimate; entering one shows each worker's pack; a bottom status bar shows live/last run state with a finish action

the tui doctor|preview|picker|policy subcommands are removed (clean cutover): doctor and policy become menu screens with unchanged behavior, picker's start flow is absorbed into Pantry, preview's role is covered by the confirmation screen and start --dry-run, and doctor --json / start --json keep serving scripted callers
in-process snapshot tests (TestBackend) cover the new screens and the confirmation gate; cargo test green in both feature configurations; CHANGELOG records the breaking change for 0.3.0

features.description: Manifest editor in the menu: create and edit manifests interactively (workers, packs, task, adapter, budget) with live fail-closed validation, format-preserving saves into a discovery dir, optional hash pins, and start --from resolving a bare manifest name against the discovery dirs
steps: editor screen: add/remove/rename workers, edit task/adapter/budget, and toggle skills from the resolved union into the focused worker's pack; validation mirrors the --from parser rules live (schema, duplicate worker names, empty packs) and blocks saving while any error is present

save writes schema-1 TOML via toml_edit — format-preserving for existing files (comments and key order outside edited arrays survive byte-for-byte) — into ./lunchbox/manifests/ or ~/.lunchbox/manifests/ (choice offered, directory created); an optional toggle saves packs as name@sha256:<64 hex> pins
start --from <name> resolves a bare name against the discovery dirs (project first, then home); a missing name fails closed listing candidates; --from <path> is unchanged
starting from the editor or menu requires the same explicit confirmation screen as feature-017; tests cover validation arms, TOML round-trip, and name resolution
